docs.dialog.a11y.dismiss: Escape and a press on the backdrop ask to close it. A drag that ends on the backdrop, such as the end of a text selection, does not.
docs.dialog.a11y.focus: When it opens, the focus moves inside. When it closes, the focus goes back to the element that had it, so a keyboard user does not lose their place.
docs.dialog.a11y.footer: Put the way to dismiss the dialog in the footer: a button labeled with the close text. Escape is a shortcut, and not everyone has it.
docs.dialog.a11y.name: The title names the dialog and the description describes it. Write a title that says what the dialog is for, and a description when the user needs more to decide.
docs.dialog.a11y.native: It is a native dialog opened as a modal: the focus stays inside it, the page behind is inert, and a screen reader announces a dialog.
docs.dialog.a11y.scroll: While it is open the scroll of the page is locked, which needs the base stylesheet of the package.
docs.dialog.a11y.strings: Dialog has no text of its own. A close button that you put in the footer and label with useFormaStrings().dialogClose follows the language of the closest FormaProvider; without one it is «Close», in English.
docs.dialog.api.children: The content between the description and the footer. It is rendered only while the dialog is open, so a form in it starts empty each time.
docs.dialog.api.className: Extra class names for the dialog element, added after the library's own. It takes no other attribute of the element.
docs.dialog.api.description: Text under the title. It becomes the accessible description of the dialog, and there is none without it.
docs.dialog.api.footer: The actions at the bottom, usually a secondary and a primary Button. Put the way to dismiss the dialog here.
docs.dialog.api.onClose: Called when the user asks to close the dialog: Escape, a press and release on the backdrop, or a native close such as a method="dialog" form. Set open to false in it: the dialog stays open until you decide. It is not called when you close the dialog by setting open yourself.
docs.dialog.api.open: Whether the dialog is open. The dialog is always in the page, and its content is rendered only while it is open.
docs.dialog.api.size: The width of the dialog: --dialog-width for default and --dialog-width-wide for wide.
docs.dialog.api.title: The title of the dialog and its accessible name.
docs.dialog.limit.close: It has no close button of its own: the footer holds the way to dismiss it.
docs.dialog.limit.content: The content is rendered only while the dialog is open, so it cannot be measured or kept in the page while it is closed.
docs.dialog.limit.controlled: It is controlled only: open is yours, and the dialog never closes itself. Forget to set it to false in onClose and Escape does nothing.
docs.dialog.limit.focusLost: If the element that had the focus is gone when the dialog closes, such as the item of a menu that unmounted, the focus falls to the page. Place it from an effect that runs when open becomes false.
docs.dialog.limit.modal: Modal is only another name for Dialog: it has no props of its own and there is no non-modal variant.
docs.dialog.limit.sizes: There are two widths and no full-screen or side-sheet variant. With prefers-reduced-motion the entrance does not move.
docs.dialog.limit.tooltip: A Tooltip on the control that takes the first focus opens while the dialog moves in and ends a few pixels off its trigger. Put another control first, or take the animation away with className.
docs.dialog.size.wideHint: It holds a field, which takes the focus when the dialog opens.
docs.dialog.sizes.description: Two widths, taken from the tokens: --dialog-width and --dialog-width-wide. Both shrink to fit a narrow window.
docs.dialog.state.defaultHint: Open it: the focus goes inside the dialog and the page behind stops responding. Escape closes it and the focus goes back to the button.
docs.dialog.state.destructiveHint: For an action that cannot be undone: the button that confirms is the danger one, and the title asks a question.
docs.dialog.states.description: A dialog is not drawn open on the page: it opens from its button, as it does in an application. Open each one with the mouse or the keyboard.
docs.dialog.strings.description: Dialog has no text of its own: a close button in the footer that reads useFormaStrings() takes its label from the closest FormaProvider, in English when there is none.
docs.dialog.strings.label: dialogClose
docs.dialog.strings.title: Built-in text
docs.dialog.summary: A modal dialog with a title, a description and actions, built on the native dialog element.
docs.dialog.usage.description: Import Dialog, keep open in your own state and set it to false in onClose. Modal is the same component under the name that Resolve gave it: import either one.
